name: Arizona

rules.summary: The county where the offense happened pays the medical or forensic exam costs to collect evidence of a sexual offense.
rules.quote: Any medical or forensic interview or examination expenses arising out of the need to secure evidence that a person has been the victim of a dangerous crime against children as defined in section 13-705 or a sexual offense pursuant to section 13-1404, 13-1405, 13-1406 or 13-3212 shall be paid by the county in which the offense occurred

rules.summary: A hospital or provider may not send the patient a balance bill for a county-paid forensic exam. The statute does not say whether the patient's insurance may be billed.
rules.quote: A health care institution or health care provider may not issue, either directly or through its billing company, any additional balance bill to a patient relating to a medical or forensic interview or examination for which the county is required to pay pursuant to section 13-1414.

rules.summary: A health care institution may not charge the patient intake, consultation, facility, or other fees as part of a county-paid forensic exam.
rules.quote: A health care institution may not charge an intake, consultation, facility or other fee to a patient as part of a medical or forensic interview or examination for which the county is required to pay pursuant to section 13-1414.

rules.summary: The maximum award is $25,000 per claim for all economic loss from one incident; each eligible person files a separate claim.
rules.quote: Twenty-five thousand dollars for all economic loss submitted under a claim as a result of an incident of criminally injurious conduct;

rules.summary: Mental health counseling and care is capped at $5,000 per victim or derivative victim.
rules.quote: For mental health counseling and care expenses, $5,000 per victim or derivative victim;

rules.summary: Work loss is limited each calendar week to 40 hours at the current minimum wage, within the overall award maximum.
rules.quote: are limited to an amount per calendar week equal to 40 hours at the current minimum wage

rules.summary: Transportation costs are capped at $2,000 per victim or derivative victim, paid as reimbursement of actual costs.
rules.quote: For transportation costs, $2,000 per victim or derivative victim paid as reimbursement of actual transportation expenses.

rules.summary: Crime scene cleanup is capped at $2,000 for professional cleanup, of which up to $500 may go to cleanup not done by a professional service.
rules.quote: For crime scene cleanup expenses, $2,000 for cleanup provided by a professional service, of which $500 may be for crime scene cleanup not provided by a professional service

rules.summary: Funeral expenses are capped at $10,000.
rules.quote: For funeral expenses, $10,000;

rules.summary: Reasonable and customary medical expenses from the victim's injury or condition are covered.
rules.quote: Reasonable and customary medical expenses due to the victim's physical injury, medical condition, mental health condition, or death.

rules.summary: Mental health counseling and care for the victim's or derivative victim's mental distress from the crime is covered, from a licensed or authorized provider.
rules.quote: Reasonable and customary mental health counseling and care expenses due to a victim's or derivative victim's mental distress resulting from the criminally injurious conduct

rules.summary: Work loss is covered when the crime's physical injury, mental distress, or medical condition reduces the victim's ability to work.
rules.quote: A victim whose ability to work is reduced due to physical injury, mental distress, or medical condition resulting from the criminally injurious conduct;

rules.summary: Transportation to get a medical forensic exam or forensic interview is covered.
rules.quote: The victim obtaining a medical forensic examination or participating in a medical forensic interview

rules.summary: Crime scene cleanup is covered for sexual assault, homicide, and aggravated assault.
rules.quote: Reasonable and customary crime scene cleanup expenses due to a victim's homicide, aggravated assault, or sexual assault

rules.summary: Crime scene cleanup includes repairing or replacing exterior doors, locks, or windows damaged by the crime at a residence.
rules.quote: Repairing or replacing exterior doors, locks, or windows damaged as a direct result of criminally injurious conduct occurring within a residence or the surrounding curtilage.
rules.pinpoint: A.A.C. R10-4-101(8)(b); covered for sexual assault under R10-4-108(C)(5)

rules.summary: Transportation costs for responding to a substantiated threat to the victim's safety or well-being are covered, within the transportation cap.
rules.quote: Responding to a substantiated threat to the safety or well-being of the victim or a derivative victim

rules.summary: Medical expense includes repairing a victim's prosthetic device, eyeglasses or corrective lenses, or dental device.
rules.quote: Repair of damage to a victim's prosthetic device, eyeglasses or other corrective lenses, or a dental device

rules.summary: The brochure says property loss or repair is not covered, nor are attorney fees or pain and suffering. The current rules still pay to repair a victim's eyeglasses, prosthetic or dental device (as medical) and damaged exterior doors, locks or windows at a residence (as crime scene cleanup).
rules.quote: The Program cannot consider claims for: • Attorney Fees • Property Loss or Repair • Pain and Suffering

rules.summary: Attorney's fees are not paid.
rules.quote: The Board shall not make a compensation award to pay attorney's fees incurred by a victim or claimant.

params.extension: The Board shall extend the deadline for good cause (R10-4-106(B)).

rules.summary: The claim must be submitted within two years after the crime is discovered; the Board extends this for good cause.
rules.quote: A claim, as described in R10-4-107, was submitted to the operational unit within two years after discovery of the criminally injurious conduct.

rules.summary: The crime must be reported to law enforcement within 72 hours after discovery. The rules list no alternative to a police report for sexual assault.
rules.quote: The criminally injurious conduct was reported to an appropriate law enforcement authority within 72 hours after its discovery;

rules.summary: The Board must extend both the reporting time limit and the filing deadline when there is good cause for the delay.
rules.quote: The Board shall extend the time limits under subsections (A)(4) and (A)(7) if the Board determines there is good cause for a delay.

rules.summary: The award is denied or reduced when the loss was or can be recovered from insurance, a government benefit, or another collateral source.
rules.quote: The Board shall deny or reduce a compensation award to a claimant if: 1. The victim or claimant has recouped or is eligible to recoup the economic loss from an obtainable and accessible collateral source, including benefits from a federal or federally financed program;

rules.summary: An award may be denied or reduced in proportion to how much the Board finds the victim responsible for the incident.
rules.quote: The Board shall deny or reduce a compensation award under subsection (F)(3) in proportion to the degree to which the Board determines the victim is responsible for the incident of criminally injurious conduct that is the subject of the claim.

rules.summary: A county program may grant one emergency award of up to $1,000 for serious hardship; it is deducted from the final award.
rules.quote: An operational unit that makes an emergency compensation award shall ensure that the emergency compensation award does not exceed $1,000.

rules.summary: Any state or federal crime that poses a substantial threat of injury, mental distress, or death qualifies, whether or not the offender is caught, charged, or convicted.
rules.quote: Constitutes a crime as defined by state or federal law regardless of whether the perpetrator of the conduct is apprehended, charged, or convicted;

params.rule: Crimes in Arizona qualify for anyone; Arizona residents hurt outside Arizona qualify only where no accessible compensation program exists.

rules.summary: The crime must have happened in Arizona, or outside Arizona to an Arizona resident in a place without an accessible compensation program.
rules.quote: Occurred in Arizona; or b. Occurred outside of Arizona in an area without an accessible crime compensation program and affected a resident;

coverage.notes: Arizona's caps and eligibility rules are in the administrative code (A.A.C. R10-4-101 to R10-4-111, final rules effective July 3, 2024; snapshot is Supp. 26-1, March 31, 2026), not the statute. No minimum loss is set in the rules. The rules list no relocation or home security expense; transportation for responding to a substantiated safety threat is covered under R10-4-108(C)(6)(e), and crime scene cleanup (sexual assault included) covers repairing exterior doors, locks, or windows damaged in the crime at a residence (R10-4-101(8)(b)). No statewide alternative to the 72-hour police report was found for sexual assault; the only relief is the Board's good-cause extension. A.R.S. 36-420.02 bars extra fees and balance bills to the patient for county-paid forensic exams but does not address billing the patient's insurance. The lost-wage cap has no fixed dollar amount (40 hours a week at the current minimum wage), so amount_cents is null. The ACJC program page body text sits inside a form element that the snapshot extractor drops, so no rule quotes it; the apply link (acjc.hostedbykarpel.com) comes from that page's HTML.

researcher_notes: Sources disagree on the filing clock: the undated ACJC brochure says to apply within two years of the crime, while A.A.C. R10-4-106(A)(7) says two years after discovery; the rule wins and is what this file uses. The application PDF linked from the ACJC page is dated June 2015 and predates the 2023/2024 rule rewrite; online filing is at acjc.hostedbykarpel.com. The program is county-run: each County Attorney's office has its own board and coordinator, and awards depend on money available to that county (R10-4-108(D)(2), (I)). A.R.S. 41-2407(E) and (F) also bar a provider who accepts program payment from billing the victim for the same service (unless the program cannot pay in full) and bar debt collection on bills included in a pending claim. Statute 13-1414 covers exams for offenses under 13-1404, 13-1405, 13-1406 and 13-3212 and dangerous crimes against children. Not used: the 2018 ACJC desk manual (predates current rules). Reviewer: the brochure also says the crime must be reported within 72 hours "of the crime"; R10-4-106(A)(4) says within 72 hours after discovery, and the rule wins. The brochure's blanket exclusion of property loss or repair is older and broader than the current rules, which pay for eyeglass/prosthetic/dental device repair (R10-4-108(C)(1)(a)(i)) and door, lock and window repair at a residence as crime scene cleanup (R10-4-101(8)(b)). R10-4-108(H)(1) requires denial for failure to cooperate with law enforcement unless the failure was due to a substantial medical, mental health, or safety risk. The forensic exam statute (A.R.S. 13-1414) covers only exam expenses arising from the need to secure evidence; follow-up medical treatment goes through the compensation claim. Filing (added Oct 3): claims go to the county program where the crime happened (A.A.C. R10-4-107(D)). Mailing addresses come from the ACJC county contact list PDF (AZ-S9), which the program page links; its 14 non-Maricopa addresses match the live program page, though several phone numbers on the PDF are older. For Maricopa the PDF lists 301 W. Jefferson, 9th Floor, but the live ACJC page and the Maricopa edition of the application (AZ-S11) say 225 West Madison Street, so the Maricopa mail rule quotes AZ-S11. The online portal (acjc.hostedbykarpel.com) is a login app that the snapshot tool cannot read, so the online rule quotes the Maricopa County Attorney page (AZ-S10), which links it for all applicants. No official source gives an email, fax, or in-person filing option. The ACJC page body (dropped by the extractor) says coordinators collect police reports, but the application and rules only ask for the report number, not a copy, so police_report is not listed as a required document. The statewide application PDF (AZ-S7, Rev. 06/2015, still the newest version) is a flat PDF with 0 AcroForm fields, and its mail-to box is a blank placeholder; the Maricopa edition is the same form with the county address filled in. Processing time is the Board's 60-day decision deadline from the rules, not a payment time.
